review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the DiscreteCoind.map simp lemmas (map_apply, coe_toCoind, coe_toCoind_symm, coe_zero) in Coinduced/Discrete.lean. I read the DiscreteShortExact simp lemmas in ShortExact.lean, and the uses of coind_incl_apply and coind_proj_apply in PreservesExactness, Shapiro/Canonical and Corestriction/ConnectingMap. The two pointwise simp lemmas have distinct heads and no competing rules. I saw no rewrite cycle, and the orientation is sensible: it pushes the coinduced map to the coefficient map on values. The only weakness I found is the lack of a field-level equation lemma. It is a modest improvement and I have not checked it by compiling. The main proofs also unfold the fields with `change` instead of the later simp lemmas, but I did not treat that as a simp-interface defect because the lemmas depend on the definition.

findings.problem: The simp interface for `coind` only has pointwise lemmas (`coind_incl_apply`, `coind_proj_apply`). There is no field-level equation saying `(coind U hU S).incl` or `.proj` is `(DiscreteCoind.map … ).toAddMonoidHom`. A comment in PreservesExactness notes that `coind` is opaque outside this module, so downstream files cannot unfold it. PreservesExactness therefore reproves the field identification by hand with `AddMonoidHom.ext`, `DiscreteCoind.ext`, `rw [coind_incl_apply]`, `change` and `rfl`. It then feeds the results to `simpa [hi, hp]`. Inside this file, the proofs of `incl_injective`, `proj_surjective` and `exact` re-derive the same unfolding with `change (DiscreteCoind.map …) g = …` followed by `rw [DiscreteCoind.map_apply …]`.
findings.proposed_change: Add two `rfl`-proved equation lemmas, `coind_incl` and `coind_proj`, after the definition. They would state `(coind U hU S).incl = (DiscreteCoind.map S.incl.toIntLinearMap S.incl_equivariant).toAddMonoidHom`, and the analogue for `proj`. Make them `@[simp]` only if the right-hand side is the intended normal form. Otherwise use them as explicit rewrite lemmas, because `simp` would lose the `coind` head that the pointwise lemmas match. The pointwise `@[simp]` lemmas stay as the canonical simp normal form on values. Downstream `hi` and `hp` and the manual `change` steps in the proofs here could then reuse these equations.
findings.benefit: The unfolding of `coind` becomes a single named rewrite instead of repeated `change` and `rfl` scripts. Downstream files that cannot see the definition body get the field description directly, so the `simpa [hi, hp]` steps need less custom plumbing.
